title: In a pushout square the cokernels of two parallel sides are isomorphic
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] and let $f:w\to y$, $g:w\to x$, $h:y\to z$, $k:x\to z$ be morphisms of $\mathcal A$ with $h\circ f=k\circ g$ such that the square is cocartesian, i.e. $(z,h,k)$ is a pushout of $f$ and $g$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $\pi_f:y\to\operatorname{Coker}(f)$ and $\pi_k:z\to\operatorname{Coker}(k)$ be cokernels. Then the unique morphism $\theta:\operatorname{Coker}(f)\to\operatorname{Coker}(k)$ with $\theta\circ\pi_f=\pi_k\circ h$ (it exists since $\pi_k\circ h\circ f=\pi_k\circ k\circ g=0$) is an isomorphism.

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: Mathlib states it for any category with zero morphisms in which the two cokernels exist (an abelian category has zero morphisms and all cokernels); take t=f, l=g, r=h, b=k, sq the pushout square (IsPushout f g h k); then cokernel.map f k g h sq.w : cokernel f -> cokernel k is the morphism theta (cokernel.π f >> theta = h >> cokernel.π k) and is an isomorphism; any other choice of cokernels differs by unique isomorphisms
